title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 104: Chairman of meetings

content.overview: Section 104 supplies the default method for electing the chairman of a company meeting, subject to the company's articles. If a poll is demanded on the election, it is taken forthwith; the show-of-hands chair remains in office until the poll elects another chair for the remainder of the meeting.
content.glance: Section 104 governs the default election and continuity of the chairman of a company meeting. The articles may provide otherwise; a poll demanded on the election is taken forthwith under the Act.
content.study:
## Statutory rule
Section 104(1) provides that, unless the articles otherwise provide, members personally present elect one of themselves as chairman by show of hands. Under section 104(2), if a poll is demanded on the election, it is taken forthwith in accordance with the Act. The person elected by show of hands continues as chairman until the poll elects another person, who chairs the remainder of the meeting.

## Application
First inspect the company's articles. If they prescribe a different method, do not assume the statutory default overrides them. If the default applies, identify the members personally present and the show-of-hands election. If a poll is demanded specifically on the election of chairman, apply the statutory continuity rule pending the poll result.

## Limits of this note
This topic-specific explanation is based on the section text. It does not independently verify company-specific exemptions, amendments, procedural rules, or case law. Check the current Act, applicable rules, notifications and articles before advising on a live meeting.

sections.heading: Default election under section 104(1)
sections.body: Unless the company's articles provide otherwise, members personally present at the meeting elect one of themselves as chairman on a show of hands. The articles must be checked before treating this as the operative method.

sections.heading: Poll demanded on the election — section 104(2)
sections.body: A poll demanded on the election of chairman is taken forthwith in accordance with the Act. The person elected by show of hands remains chairman until the poll result elects another person.

sections.heading: Effect of the poll result
sections.body: If the poll elects a different person, that person chairs the meeting for its remaining duration. The poll rule is specifically about election of the chairman; do not extend it to unrelated voting questions without separate authority.

sections.heading: Practical record and source check
sections.body: Read the articles, notice and meeting record; record the method of election, any demand for a poll, and the poll result. Company-specific exemptions, applicable rules and current amendments require separate verification.

examples.body: The articles do not prescribe another method. Members personally present elect one of themselves as chair by show of hands. On these assumed facts, the default in section 104(1) governs.

examples.title: Articles provide otherwise
examples.body: The articles prescribe a different method for choosing the chairman. The statutory default is expressly subject to the articles, so the articles must be analysed before concluding that an election by show of hands is required.

hypotheticals.question: A chair is elected by show of hands and a poll is demanded on that election. Who chairs while the poll is pending, and after it concludes?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under section 104(2), the poll is taken forthwith. The show-of-hands chair continues until the poll elects another person; any person elected by the poll chairs the remainder of the meeting. Confirm first that the articles do not provide otherwise.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the show-of-hands method as unconditional.
misconceptions.correction: Section 104(1) begins with an express qualification: the company's articles may provide otherwise.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming the show-of-hands chairman immediately ceases to chair when a poll is demanded.
misconceptions.correction: Under section 104(2), the existing chairman continues until the poll elects another person; the newly elected person chairs the remainder of the meeting.

misconceptions.trap: Applying section 104 to every meeting without checking scope and company-specific rules.
misconceptions.correction: Check the current Act, applicable rules, notifications and the company's articles before giving meeting-specific advice.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What facts must be checked before advising on a disputed chairman election?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Inspect the articles; identify the members personally present and the election method; determine whether a poll was demanded specifically on the chairman's election; record the poll result; and verify applicable rules, exemptions and current amendments.
